title: Essential metrics slice + tiered launch plan for Console dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a trimmed, high-impact MVP for Console observability features (dashboards, traces, cost breakdown) so we can ship a usable product in the next release window and validate customer value before investing in full feature parity. This ticket captures scope decisions, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and follow-ups for the "Essential metrics" slice.

Context and goals:
- Customers repeatedly ask for quick visibility into cost drivers, top error paths, and latency hotspots without waiting for a full telemetry surface.
- Full feature set (token-level cost drilldowns, user-level RBAC filtering, full-span waterfall traces) is out of scope for MVP due to backend complexity and infra risk.
- Goal: ship a focused console surface that delivers 80% of customer value for ~20% of the effort.

MVP scope (what we will ship):
1) Dashboards: a small set of curated cards (6 total) covering customer-facing SLOs: request rate, error rate (5xx), p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k requests (model-aggregated), top 5 endpoints by cost, and system health (infra utilization). Cards are configurable but only support two time ranges (1h, 24h) for MVP.
2) Tracing: integrated trace samples surfaced for routes with elevated error rate or p95 latency. MVP shows a single representative span timeline and top 3 contributing services. Sampling fixed at 1% by default and adjustable via a global knob (no per-customer sampling rules). No full waterfall trace UI in MVP — we link to raw trace explorer for advanced debugging.
3) Cost breakdown: simplified model-level cost attribution per route (model name + route). No token-level breakdown, no per-user billing export. Cost estimates are generated via aggregation of token counters and pricing profiles, surfaced as daily totals and 7-day trend.
4) Rollouts and fallbacks: feature-flagged experience with canary rollout to 10% of eligible orgs, automatic rollback on error or excessive backend latency.

Explicit out-of-scope for MVP (deferred):
- Token-level or per-user billing views
- Fine-grained RBAC filters or per-team dashboards
- Custom chart builder, alerting rules, and full trace waterfall visualization
- Long-term storage/retention beyond 30 days (analytics archive)

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Keeping sampling coarse (1%) reduces backend storage and query costs but increases risk of missing rare failure modes; we mitigate by boosting sampling for routes in the detection window.
- Aggregating cost at model+route level avoids heavy joins with billing pipelines and lets us provide early actionable recommendations (e.g., move to a lower cost model). It limits granularity but dramatically shortens time-to-delivery.
- Limiting time ranges reduces UI complexity and performance surface area for early customers.

Acceptance criteria (all must be satisfied for "Done"):
- Functional:
  * Dashboard page loads under 2.5s (cold) and under 1.2s (warm) for orgs with < 5k daily requests.
  * All 6 MVP cards render and reflect data for 1h and 24h ranges; empty-state copy present when no data.
  * Trace preview opens for selected high-error routes and shows the representative span timeline with service attribution.
  * Cost breakdown displays per-route and per-model daily totals for the last 7 days.
- Accuracy and reliability:
  * Cost estimates for model+route are within ±15% of billing-derived numbers over a 7-day window for test orgs.
  * Telemetry ingestion success rate >= 95% for accepted events under normal load.
  * Console backend query p95 latency < 300ms for single-card reads under expected load (synthetic load tests).
- UX and QA:
  * Product / Design sign-off on final card layouts and trace preview (mockups approved).
  * Accessibility: basic keyboard nav and color contrast pass internal a11y checklist.
  * End-to-end tests covering: dashboard load, time-range switch, trace open, cost card accuracy.
- Launch and rollout:
  * Feature-flag controls implemented and accessible for rollout team.
  * Automated health checks and SLO alarms configured; canary to 10% orgs for 48 hours and rollback criteria documented.

Implementation plan (high level tasks):
- Backend engineering: implement model+route cost aggregation job, expose consolidated metrics API (ENG-2745).
- Tracing infra: add deterministic 1% sampler + detection escalation when p95/error thresholds hit (ENG-3321).
- Frontend: build Dashboard shell + 6 MVP cards, trace preview modal, simple cost table (DESIGN mocks: Confluence link).
- QA/Load: synthetic load tests, cost-accuracy validation against billing exports.
- Telemetry: ensure event enrichment includes model and route tags.

Acceptance test steps (for QA):
1) Deploy feature flag to staging and enable for test org.
2) Inject synthetic traffic with known model mix and token lengths for 7 days; export billing numbers.
3) Validate dashboard cards reflect injected signals (counts, p95, errors).
4) Validate cost card aggregated totals match billing within ±15%.
5) Induce an error spike and confirm trace preview surfaces the representative span.

Rollout strategy and monitoring:
- Canary: 10% of eligible orgs for 48 hours. Monitor: telemetry ingestion rate, console query latency, error rate, cost-estimate divergence.
- If any of: telemetry rate < 90%, console query p95 > 500ms, cost divergence > 25% for >10% of sampled orgs => automatic rollback.

Follow-ups (post-MVP / future):
- Add token-level cost drilling and per-user exports.
- Per-org sampling rules and per-route retention policies.
- Custom alerting and chart builder.
- Longer retention and cross-org rollups for enterprise customers.
